_comment: Written by the trading runs. impliedMove is a decimal or null. null means the straddle was not pulled - an open checklist item, not a placeholder to guess at. This file is a list of what is AHEAD: the pre-close run prunes catalysts once their date has passed and re-reads spot from a live quote, because a reference price carried from the day it was written makes every implied range wrong.
prunedNote: PRE-CLOSE PRUNE. NOTHING REMOVED, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME RATHER THAN A SKIPPED STEP: the file holds one row, SMCI on 8/11, and 8/11 is still ahead. Nothing on this board's other eleven names has a catalyst in the forward window - the calendar was swept live at 934 events across 8/10 to 8/14 and SMCI is the only watched name in it - so the file is complete as well as current. WHAT THIS PASS ACTUALLY CHANGED IS THE PAIR OF NUMBERS THE ROW RESTS ON, AND IT CHANGED THEM TOGETHER. spot goes from the 09:46 bid of 32.52 to the live 15:35 bid of 31.70, and rather than refresh a reference price while leaving the ratio struck against a spot that no longer exists, the straddle was re-pulled at the same moment: the 8/14 32 call marks 2.025 and the 32 put 2.330, a 4.355 straddle on a 31.70 spot, so impliedMove moves from 0.142 to 0.137. A spot refreshed on its own would have made the row internally inconsistent in the flattering direction, which is the failure this file's own comment warns about. THE COMPOSITION FLIPPED AND IT IS NOT A SIGNAL. At 09:45 the call marked above the put, 2.51 against 2.05; now the put marks above the call, 2.330 against 2.025. That is spot crossing the 32 strike - 32.21 above it this morning, 31.70 below it now - and not the market taking a side. The deltas say so directly: 0.511 on the call against -0.489 on the put is as close to symmetric as this chain gets. Recorded because a flipped straddle composition reads like a directional tell if nobody checks which of the two things moved. THE REFUSAL IS UNCHANGED AND WAS NEVER CLOSE. 13.7% is a smaller number than 14.2% and it is the same answer: an 8% equity stop sits entirely inside a 13.7% expected move, so the realistic bad case gaps through the stop rather than filling at it. Half a point of implied move does not reach the gap between 8 and 13.7.

moves.source: Straddle re-pulled live at 15:35 ET on 8/10 by the pre-close, at the same moment as the spot it is divided by. The SMCI 2026-08-14 32 call marks 2.025 (2.00 bid / 2.05 ask, 2,399 open interest, delta 0.511) and the 32 put marks 2.330 (2.31 bid / 2.35 ask, 645 open interest, delta -0.489), a 4.355 straddle against the live 31.70 bid - 13.7%, recorded here as 0.137. This replaces the 09:45 reading of 4.56 against a 32.21 spot, 0.142, which was correct when struck and whose spot is now six hours old. The call/put composition inverted between the two readings because spot crossed the 32 strike, not because the market took a side; near-symmetric deltas confirm it. Calendar re-verified live at 15:35 against 934 events across 8/10 to 8/14: 8/11, timing pm, verified true, no actual, estimate 0.88, and still the only watched name reporting inside the window.

branches.cond: An equity entry considered on SMCI before the 8/11 close
branches.act: Refused. The number was re-pulled and it refuses the trade again.
branches.why: Item 3 is satisfied by a straddle struck at the same moment as the spot it is divided by, and it decides against the trade rather than merely permitting it to be considered. A 13.7% implied move against the rulebook's -8% equity stop means the stop sits entirely inside the event: the realistic bad case gaps through it rather than filling at it, so the exit written before entry would not be the exit taken. The morning reading was 14.2% and this one is 13.7%; half a point does not close a gap between 8 and 13.7, and the refusal never depended on the third decimal. This is a mechanical refusal, not a view on whether the report is good.

branches.cond: An option considered on this name at any time before the print
branches.act: Refused outright, and it was never reachable
branches.why: The rulebook forbids holding an option through a print - IV crush kills even a correct call - and any 3-6 week expiry from here necessarily spans 8/11. The straddle does not enter into it; this branch closes on the calendar alone, which was re-verified live at 15:35. The 8/14 contracts quoted above are the straddle used to price the event and are not themselves proposable: four days to expiry is inside the three-week floor twice over.

branches.cond: SMCI still wanted after the print
branches.act: Re-approach from 8/12, on the reaction bar rather than into it
branches.why: The post-print session is the first point at which this name is available to the rulebook at all, and item 2 will then govern: the reaction day is not the entry, the day-2/3 pullback that holds is. Recorded now so a post-print entry is a decision made in advance rather than a reflex on the day.
